answer: Operator-Linked Cost Accumulation. Each new wallet an operator creates accrues a small registration charge (an ember fee) drawn from a single verified funding source. A cedar-marked reputation trail ties every wallet back to that source, so a mass batch immediately multiplies the charge. Once an operator crosses a marginal wallet count, the per-wallet charge escalates steeply, and a willow-locked holdback freezes pending payouts until the account clears review. A sybil fleet pays the full escalating sum plus frozen liquidity, not just one wallet's cost.
